name: MMLU
description: Massive Multitask Language Understanding evaluates broad subject knowledge across 57 academic and professional domains.
measures: General knowledge, domain recall, and multiple-choice reasoning.
evaluation: Models answer multiple-choice questions; the headline score is accuracy.

name: MMLU-Pro
description: MMLU-Pro extends MMLU with harder, reasoning-focused questions and more answer choices.
measures: Robust academic reasoning across 14 domains.
evaluation: Models answer multiple-choice questions; the headline score is overall accuracy.

name: GPQA
description: GPQA contains graduate-level, Google-proof science questions written by domain experts.
measures: Difficult scientific reasoning in biology, chemistry, and physics.
evaluation: Models answer multiple-choice questions; the headline score is accuracy, often on GPQA Diamond.

name: Humanity's Last Exam
description: Humanity's Last Exam is a broad expert-level benchmark covering many hard academic and professional topics.
measures: Frontier reasoning and knowledge on questions intended to remain hard for advanced AI systems.
evaluation: Models answer expert-written questions; published leaderboards report aggregate accuracy.

name: ARC-AGI
description: ARC-AGI evaluates adaptation to novel abstract reasoning tasks rather than memorized knowledge.
measures: Fluid intelligence, abstraction, and adaptation under a task budget.
evaluation: Systems solve held-out ARC tasks; the headline score is task success rate.

name: SimpleBench
description: SimpleBench targets deceptively simple reasoning problems that are still difficult for frontier models.
measures: Everyday reasoning, spatial-temporal reasoning, social reasoning, and trick-resistant comprehension.
evaluation: Models answer a fixed set of multiple-choice questions; the headline score is accuracy.

name: HumanEval
description: HumanEval evaluates whether models can synthesize Python functions that pass hidden unit tests.
measures: Code generation correctness on small programming tasks.
evaluation: Generated code is executed against tests; leaderboards usually report pass@1.

name: MBPP
description: MBPP evaluates Python program synthesis on short, crowd-sourced programming problems.
measures: Basic coding ability and unit-test correctness.
evaluation: Generated programs are executed against test cases; leaderboards usually report pass@1.

name: LiveCodeBench
description: LiveCodeBench evaluates coding ability on continuously updated programming problems.
measures: Code generation and problem solving on recent programming tasks.
evaluation: Generated solutions are executed against tests; the updater averages official per-problem pass@1 rows.

name: Aider Polyglot
description: Aider's polyglot benchmark tests code editing across C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, and Rust.
measures: Code editing accuracy across languages.
evaluation: Models edit repositories; the headline score is percent correct.

name: BigCodeBench
description: BigCodeBench evaluates code generation on practical and library-rich programming tasks.
measures: Instruction-following code generation and completion quality.
evaluation: Generated code is executed against tests; this tracker uses the best available official pass@1 field per model.

name: SWE-bench Verified
description: SWE-bench Verified is a human-filtered subset of real software engineering issues.
measures: Repository understanding, patch generation, and test-passing issue resolution.
evaluation: Agents submit patches for 500 verified tasks; the headline score is percent resolved.

name: SWE-bench Live
description: SWE-bench Live is an automatically updating SWE-bench-like benchmark for current software tasks.
measures: Agentic issue resolution on newer, multi-language, multi-OS software tasks.
evaluation: Agents submit patches; published results report percent resolved.

name: Terminal-Bench
description: Terminal-Bench evaluates agents on realistic terminal-based tasks.
measures: Shell use, tool use, debugging, and multi-step task execution.
evaluation: Agents work in terminal environments; official leaderboards report task success.

name: TAU-Bench
description: TAU-Bench evaluates language agents interacting with users and tools in realistic domains.
measures: Tool use, instruction following, policy compliance, and multi-turn task success.
evaluation: Agents complete simulated user tasks; leaderboards report pass or success rates.

name: OSWorld
description: OSWorld evaluates multimodal agents operating real desktop applications.
measures: Computer control, visual grounding, and end-to-end desktop task completion.
evaluation: Agents interact with a computer environment; official results report task success.

name: WebArena
description: WebArena evaluates autonomous agents on realistic web-based tasks.
measures: Browser navigation, planning, and web tool use.
evaluation: Agents complete tasks on instrumented websites; leaderboards report task success.

name: WebVoyager
description: WebVoyager evaluates multimodal web agents on real websites.
measures: Visual web grounding, browser actions, and task completion.
evaluation: Agents complete web tasks; published results report success rate.

name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard
description: BFCL evaluates tool and function calling across live and non-live tool-use scenarios.
measures: Function selection, argument construction, relevance, and multi-turn tool use.
evaluation: Models produce function calls; official CSVs report aggregate accuracy.

name: ToolAthlon
description: ToolAthlon, also described as Tool Decathlon, evaluates agents using diverse realistic tools.
measures: Tool selection, sequencing, execution, and long-horizon completion.
evaluation: Agents execute tasks across software environments; published results report success scores.

name: MCP Atlas
description: MCP Atlas evaluates tool-use competency across real Model Context Protocol servers and tools.
measures: Multi-server tool coordination, tool selection, and agent workflow completion.
evaluation: Agents complete MCP-backed tasks; public leaderboards report pass rate.

name: LongBench
description: LongBench evaluates long-context understanding across single-document, multi-document, and code tasks.
measures: Long-context comprehension, retrieval, summarization, and reasoning.
evaluation: Models answer long-context tasks; leaderboards report average score.

name: RULER
description: RULER evaluates long-context models using configurable synthetic retrieval and reasoning tasks.
measures: Needle retrieval, variable tracking, aggregation, and long-context robustness.
evaluation: Models answer synthetic long-context tasks; reports aggregate accuracy by context length.

name: Needle In A Haystack
description: Needle In A Haystack tests whether a model can retrieve a hidden fact from long contexts.
measures: Long-context recall and retrieval at different depths and lengths.
evaluation: Models answer questions about inserted facts; reports retrieval accuracy over depth and length.

name: MMMU
description: MMMU evaluates college-level multimodal understanding across many disciplines.
measures: Vision-language reasoning, charts, diagrams, and domain knowledge.
evaluation: Models answer multimodal multiple-choice or short-answer questions; headline score is accuracy.

name: AI2D
description: AI2D evaluates visual question answering on science diagrams.
measures: Diagram understanding and visual reasoning.
evaluation: Models answer questions about diagrams; leaderboards report accuracy.

name: DocVQA
description: DocVQA evaluates visual question answering over document images.
measures: OCR, document layout understanding, and grounded question answering.
evaluation: Models answer document questions; official evaluations report ANLS-style scores.

name: OmniDocBench
description: OmniDocBench evaluates document understanding and parsing across diverse layouts.
measures: OCR, layout parsing, formula/table understanding, and document reasoning.
evaluation: Systems parse and answer over document data; published results use composite metrics.
